---
title: "Collaborator workflow"
---

## Working agreement {#sec-working-agreement}

Start with the small CPU case, run the tests, and read the physics/notation
pages before changing units or clocks. Keep one physical change per comparison.
Preserve failed runs and negative results. Do not change an acceptance tolerance
after seeing a discrepancy without documenting why.

The four libraries are bundled source packages, not disposable caches. A
kernel change belongs under the owning `lib/` package; configuration and run
orchestration belong under `src/`; command-line wrappers belong under `scripts/`.
Do not introduce hidden sibling-checkout or machine-specific paths.

## Local development loop {#sec-development-loop}

```sh
julia --project=. -t auto scripts/bootstrap.jl --backend=cpu
julia --project=. -t auto test/runtests.jl
julia --project=. -t auto scripts/run_pmf.jl examples/cosmology-smoke.toml \
  --backend=cpu --output=results/change-check
uv sync --extra test
uv run python -m unittest discover -s test/python -v
```

Add a regression test next to the behavior you change. Numerical work should
include a controlled solution/limit, a resolution or timestep comparison where
relevant, positivity/conservation diagnostics, and backend parity at comparable
precision. A long run without a crash does not replace a small diagnostic test.

For a GPU change, bootstrap its optional environment and run
`scripts/test_gpu.jl` on real hardware. Avoid running another all-memory GPU
campaign concurrently. Record unavailable devices as untested.

## Kernel conventions {#sec-kernel-conventions}

- Keep device computations allocation-free and precision-generic where the
  algorithm supports it. Avoid implicit Float64 constants in a Float32-only
  Metal path.
- Preserve conserved/primitive variable ordering, grid staggering, boundary
  conditions, derivative symbols, and transform normalization.
- Synchronize for timings and host reads; asynchronous launches alone cannot
  establish elapsed compute time or a valid output state.
- Keep the cube/reference paths consistent when changing reconstruction,
  Riemann dispatch, or source-aware updates.
- Test reductions, view offsets, channel batching, and cache/device ownership
  explicitly when changing transform code.
- Report source-cadence, positivity fallback, projection, and thermal-floor
  changes as numerical changes, not just optimizations.

## A reproducible contribution {#sec-contribution-record}

Include the source fingerprint, Julia version, dependency manifest, backend and
hardware, exact command, input TOML, resolved environment, output epochs,
comparison observables, tolerances, and raw evidence. For performance, include
the [measurement definition](performance.qmd#sec-performance-definitions).

For an issue, supply a minimal configuration, `run.log`, metadata, expected and
observed behavior, and whether it reproduces on CPU. Remove private paths or
data before publishing logs. Never upload large checkpoints as ordinary Git
blobs; use an appropriately licensed archived dataset and record its checksum.

## Documentation build {#sec-doc-build}

Requires Quarto 1.7+ and Python 3.11+. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s docs/scripts -p 'test_*.py'
quarto render docs --fail-if-warnings
python3 docs/scripts/check_links.py docs/_site
quarto preview docs --no-browser
```

The render pre-hook builds revision metadata, checked local source pages, the
complete driver-option index, and evidence includes. Julia is **not** rerun by
rendering. The link checker validates local pages, assets, and fragments; it
does not promise that remote literature or repository URLs are reachable.

Every evaluated equation needs a checked `src` link. Tests are linked as
**test source**, not marked as passing unless an actual evidence record supports
that conclusion. Make linked sections/equations explicit anchors. Keep notation,
limitations, and status current when behavior changes. The actual adaptation
of the Quadrant template is recorded in `docs/README.md`.

## Pages deployment {#sec-pages}

`.github/workflows/pages.yml` tests documentation tooling, renders the book,
checks local links, uploads `docs/_site`, and deploys the Pages artifact on main.
Pull requests build and check without deploying. It does not push a `gh-pages`
branch or execute numerical validation on GitHub-hosted hardware.

A repository maintainer must select **GitHub Actions** as the Pages source and
allow the `github-pages` environment deployment. No local documentation command
changes repository settings. The workflow follows the
[GitHub custom-workflow deployment contract](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages)
and [Quarto's GitHub Pages guidance](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html).

## Updating extracted sources {#sec-refresh}

Source provenance is recorded in `provenance/extraction.json`; portable Python
tools maintain a separate `tools/reference/provenance.json`. Retain upstream
attribution, source hashes, and working-tree modifications. Refresh an extracted
component deliberately and review its diff; do not overwrite local scientific
fixes or regenerate unrelated files as part of a docs change.

Before a release, resolve the [license and attribution boundary](status.qmd#sec-attribution),
rerun current extraction tests, collect each hardware record you intend to claim,
and archive the full science-convergence artifacts separately from unit tests.
